title: RFID Card Manufacturer in China — Factory-Direct
summary: Proud Tek is a factory-direct RFID card manufacturer in Shenzhen, China — building cards in-house since 2008 and shipping to buyers in 50+ countries — that owns the whole card line end to end: inlay assembly, hot-roll lamination, die-cutting to the ISO/IEC 7810 ID-1 (CR80) format, printing, encoding and 100% electrical test, across PVC, PET, PETG, ABS, polycarbonate, PLA, bamboo-composite, wood and metal bodies. 'Manufacturer' here means the chip, the antenna, the card body and the data are all handled under one ISO 9001 quality system — not a logo printed on someone else's stock. This page walks the production line stage by stage, the card families and chips we laminate across LF, HF and UHF, the materials and finishes, and the MOQ, lead-time and QC records a procurement team checks before the first order.
heroPoints: One factory owns the entire card — inlay assembly, hot-roll lamination, die-cutting, offset and digital printing, encoding and 100% electrical test all run on Proud Tek's own Shenzhen lines, not subcontracted to a converter down the road.

The full card catalogue from one supplier: LF 125 kHz, HF 13.56 MHz and UHF chip families laminated into PVC, PETG, ABS, polycarbonate, PLA, bamboo-composite, wood, transparent and metal bodies — all built to ISO/IEC 7810 card dimensions.

A qualifying path built for procurement — a free sample kit, a low-MOQ pilot, then locked-price production, with ISO 9001 / 14001 / 45001 certificates, per-shipment compliance paperwork and factory-audit access you can verify before you commit.

sections.title: What a factory-direct card manufacturer controls
sections.intro: 'Card manufacturer' gets claimed by trading desks that never touch a lamination roll, so the honest test is which steps a supplier actually owns. Proud Tek owns all of them: we assemble the inlay, laminate the [card body](/products/rfid-cards/), die-cut it to ISO/IEC 7810 dimensions, print it, encode it and read-test every piece — the whole chain on our own Shenzhen lines since 2008. For the security-grade end of the range there is a dedicated [smart-card manufacturing page](/lp/rfid-smart-card-manufacturer/), and for volume economics the [bulk-card page](/lp/bulk-rfid-cards/); this page is the factory itself. The numbers below are the ones a procurement team checks first.
bullets: Full in-house production — inlay assembly, hot-roll lamination, die-cutting, offset and digital printing, encoding and 100% electrical test under one roof, so one team is accountable from PO to dispatch rather than five subcontractors.
Direct chip allocation from the major card-chip makers (NXP, Infineon, Fudan) with authorised-distribution backup, so a card program is not held hostage to one vendor's lead time.

A direct factory, not a trading desk: two Shenzhen sites, ten automated lines and 305+ pieces of process equipment under one ISO 9001 management system, every encoded card read-tested before it ships.

Export-ready fulfilment — ISO/IEC 7810, 14443 and 15693 conformance, per-shipment RoHS / REACH / FCC / CE paperwork, FOB Shenzhen / Yantian or DDP terms, and English-speaking project managers who reply within one business day.

sections.title: How an RFID card is actually made — five production stages
sections.intro: Every Proud Tek card runs the same five stages, documented on a production traveller from PO to dispatch — and knowing them lets you read a quotation line by line, because each cost item maps to one stage. The [factory encoding step](/lp/rfid-card-encoding-service/) and the [printing step](/lp/custom-rfid-card-printing/) each have a page of their own; here is how they sit in the line. The operators who run your 100-piece pilot are the same ones who run the 100,000-piece order.

image.alt: A five-stage RFID card production line, left to right. Stage 1, inlay assembly: chip bonded to antenna at HF 13.56 MHz and UHF, failed inlays scrapped. Stage 2, collate and laminate: inlays sandwiched between card-body layers and hot-roll laminated at around 150°C. Stage 3, die-cut: punched to the ISO/IEC 7810 ID-1 CR80 format, 85.60 by 53.98 by 0.76 mm. Stage 4, print and finish: offset, digital, screen, hot stamping and laser engraving. Stage 5, encode and test: data written on the line and every card given a 100% functional read test before packing.

items.label: 1. Inlay assembly
items.text: The chip is bonded to an etched or wire antenna in-house (HF 13.56 MHz and UHF wet-inlay assembly), and any inlay that fails a readability check is scrapped before it ever reaches card production.

items.label: 2. Collate & laminate
items.text: Inlays are sandwiched between card-body layers and hot-roll laminated under controlled heat, pressure and dwell — around 150°C — permanently encapsulating chip and antenna into a single monolithic card.

items.label: 3. Die-cut to CR80
items.text: Laminated sheets are punched to the ISO/IEC 7810 ID-1 (CR80) format, 85.60 × 53.98 × 0.76 mm — the payment-card footprint, so finished cards fit every standard reader, hotel lock and badge printer.

items.label: 4. Print & finish
items.text: Four-colour offset for volume, digital for short runs, plus screen printing, hot stamping, laser engraving, signature panels, hologram and magnetic-stripe options — the full finish menu lives on the card-printing page.

items.label: 5. Encode & 100% test
items.text: UID read, NDEF or sector data written on the line, then a functional read test on every encoded card — chip response, antenna resonance and read range — before it is packed.

sections.title: Card body materials we laminate
sections.intro: Material drives feel, durability and price more than any line item except the chip, and every stock in our range earns its place — wallet thinness, a sustainability mandate, a premium unboxing or a pool-deck beating. All of them run on the same lamination lines, so mixing materials across a program does not mean mixing suppliers. The points below are the stocks buyers ask for most.
bullets: PVC — the standard card body: lowest cost, full-bleed print compatibility and years of normal wallet service. The volume default unless a requirement pushes elsewhere.
PETG and ABS — tougher and more temperature-tolerant than PVC, specified for gym, pool, locker and other high-handling environments.
Polycarbonate — the decade-of-daily-use option, laser-engravable for tamper-resistant personalisation on government and enterprise credentials.

PLA, recycled-PVC and FSC-certified paper — lower-footprint bodies for sustainability mandates, with RoHS and REACH SVHC declarations on file by SKU; FSC paper and bamboo-composite offered on request for chain-of-custody programs.

Wood and bamboo — laser-engravable natural stocks for hotel-key and premium-membership programs; see the [wooden card](/products/rfid-cards/rfid-wooden-card/) and [bamboo card](/products/rfid-cards/rfid-bamboo-card/) SKU pages.

Transparent and metal — clear PET for promotional cards, and stainless-steel bodies for premium business cards; metal detunes a 13.56 MHz antenna, so metal cards use a slot-antenna design to stay readable.

faq.question: How do I verify your card factory before I place an order?
faq.answer: Three independent checks. First, request our ISO 9001, ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 certificate numbers and confirm them directly with the issuing registrar. Second, book a factory audit — engineering and quality-system audits across our two Shenzhen sites are by appointment, with virtual walk-throughs for buyers who cannot travel and third-party (SGS, TUV, Intertek) inspection when your program requires it. Third, order a free sample kit and read the cards on your own equipment. Every claim on this page is meant to be checked, not taken on faith.

faq.question: What is the minimum order quantity for RFID cards, and can I sample first?
faq.answer: Free samples come first: a 5-10 card kit ships by courier so you can verify chip compatibility and print quality before buying. For production, custom-printed PVC cards start at 500 pieces, digital-print short runs at 100 pieces, and metal or specialty-material cards at 200 pieces; recurring programs typically run 1,000-5,000 pieces per SKU. Volume price breaks are detailed on the bulk-card page.

faq.question: How long does card production and shipping take from China?
faq.answer: Standard production is 5-7 business days after artwork approval, with express production for urgent orders. Shipping to North America and Europe is 3-5 days by express courier or 15-25 days by sea freight for large volumes on FOB Shenzhen / Yantian terms — roughly 10-14 days door-to-door for an express order.

faq.question: Can you match or replace an RFID card from another supplier?
faq.answer: Yes. Send a sample card or its specifications — chip type, frequency, memory size, artwork and dimensions — and we will produce an exact match or recommend an improved alternative. Our engineers can read the existing card's chip data to identify the IC and replicate the encoding format, then read-verify the replacement against your reader.

faq.question: Which card material and chip family should I choose?
faq.answer: Match the body to the environment and the chip to the interaction. PVC suits most programs; PETG, ABS or polycarbonate suit heavy handling and long service; wood, bamboo and recycled stocks suit premium or sustainability programs. For chips, HF 13.56 MHz (MIFARE, NTAG) covers access and tap cards, LF 125 kHz (EM4100, T5577) covers legacy access, and UHF covers long-range identification; security-grade selection is covered on the smart-card page. A mixed sample kit lets you decide on the evidence.
